long_biography.plain_text:
EW Healthcare Partners grew from investment platforms Marty Sutter built in Texas. He established a venture-capital company inside Mitchell Energy, then formed the independent Woodlands Venture Partners in 1988. Its merger with Essex Venture Partners in 1994 created Essex Woodlands, later renamed EW Healthcare Partners.

Sutter has combined capital allocation with active development of healthcare businesses. He has participated in more than 30 portfolio companies, several later acquired by major medical groups. At EW, he led the investment behind Bioventus, formed by spinning a clinical-therapies division out of Smith & Nephew, and worked with its management on subsequent growth initiatives.
